en.html:
......After that, a little over two weeks passed like a gale.

I talked the senior house round.
Grudgingly, they gave their permission for the masterless warriors to settle.

With my foster mother beside me, I explained everything to the townspeople.
Most of them were glad to hear it.

I got no chance to meet the leader, who had gone back to the mountain, but the 'bandit' raids stopped completely.

The town had its peace back, after quite some time.
The senior house admitted that I had contributed to it,

and, as promised, arranged to bring a doctor from Germany.

And then.
With a great many instruments and assistants, the famous doctor arrived in our little country town in Yamato—

en.html:
Hikaru's symptoms had visibly improved. The fallen hair and the stripped-away flesh had not returned, but the shadow of death that used to follow her everywhere, that air of despair, had gone somewhere else.

No animal groaning came from her mouth any more. Her breathing was very calm.

...But.
Her eyes alone had not changed.

Dark.
Empty.
Looking at nothing.

Twin eyes the color of glass, with no sign of where the mind was kept.
Those were exactly as before.

en.html:
A miracle.

I had never thought deeply about that word. Today was the first day.

And I noticed something. Miracle: a pleasant-sounding word. For the person who has no need of it, it is like winter clothing in the middle of summer, a reassuring guarantee that you will survive the cold whenever winter finally comes.

For the person who needs it, it is a useless sweater locked in the almirah, whose key you discover missing only after winter has started. You stand there stunned, learning that it was out of reach all along.

It is never a sign of where hope is.
Quite the reverse.

What a miracle shows is...
the hopeless distance between you and it.

としない者にとっては言うなれば夏場の冬着――いつ
か訪れる冬の寒さに耐える力を保証する心強いもので。

を失くしたことに気付いて取り出せずにいる無意味な
<ruby>編服<rt>セーター</rt></ruby>のようなものだ。

　奇跡が示すものは……
　そこに至るまでの、絶望的な距離だ。

A miracle.
How does one even get hold of one? I did not know.

I did not know what I should do. Until now I had a clear aim: bring Doctor Mengele. After the promise to the senior house, the means to that aim, settling the bandit problem, became the aim itself.

Now I had no aim.
No. The aim was there, but I could not see the road to it.

What should I do to...
bring back Hikaru's mind?

...In the first place,
could it really be brought back?

　　　　　—Why was I not called earlier—

en.html:
Having no other words, I said it again.
A useless, meaningless apology.

The Minato house took me in and kept alive, for more than twenty years, a life that should have ended beside the road. That debt is beyond description.

And how little I had repaid it. I could not even save the household's precious heir.

Even a freeloader has limits, and I was past them. Why was I not born as a somewhat more useful creature? If a human being's measure did not suit me, cattle would have been fine.

Set beside a man who only eats free rice, any cow or horse in the neighborhood is hundreds of times more worthwhile.
en.text:
Having no other words, I said it again.
A useless, meaningless apology.

The Minato house took me in and kept alive, for more than twenty years, a life that should have ended beside the road. That debt is beyond description.

And how little I had repaid it. I could not even save the household's precious heir.

Even a freeloader has limits, and I was past them. Why was I not born as a somewhat more useful creature? If a human being's measure did not suit me, cattle would have been fine.

Set beside a man who only eats free rice, any cow or horse in the neighborhood is hundreds of times more worthwhile.

他に言葉がなく、そう口にする。
　益体もない、無意味な謝罪を。

　湊斗家に引き取られ、路傍に果てるべき命を生かさ
れて二十余年。
　その恩は形容しようもなく大きい。

　それに対して、俺の報いるところの少なさたるや。
　大事な家督継承者を救うことさえできなかった。

　穀潰しにも程がある。
　どうして俺は、もう少し役に立つ生物として生まれ
てこなかったのか。人間の器量に相応しくないなら、
別に家畜でも構わなかった。

　無駄飯を食うだけの男に比べれば、その辺りの牛馬
の方が何百倍も有意義だろう……。

en.html:
Unlike her fist, my foster mother's scolding was gentle. All the same, it woke me up.

Giving up.
...Had I given up?

To despair at my own powerlessness meant deciding that nothing was left for me to do. That is giving up.

Absurd.
I had no right to give up.

If only my own life were involved, abandoning it or throwing it away might be my business. But what was staked here was Hikaru's life.

How could I throw it away on my own say-so? Hikaru had endured this entire year with a vitality that amazed even the doctor!

Thinking of that, even the time spent hanging my head seemed wasted. If I had time to spare for that, then—

　諦め。

　自分の無力に絶望するという事はつまり、
　自分にはもう何もできないと、諦めるという事。

　諦めていい筈がない。

　俺の人生なら、諦めるのも投げるのも俺の勝手かも
しれない。

　そう思えば、項垂れている暇さえ惜しい。
　そんな余裕があるなら――

統"You are going to save Hikaru. Me and you."
Kageaki"Yes."
統"You are saving her. Because of you, Hikaru's body is better for now."
Kageaki"..."
統"Thank you, I will not say. Apne ghar ki baat hai. She's family. Naturally we do this."
Kageaki"Yes...!"
統"We see it through. And listen to me: you haven't gone backward. You haven't rolled all the way down either."
統"You are moving forward. Believe that much."
Kageaki"..."
統"Now you stand here looking behind you—hai, should have taken that other road. What will come of that? Aage dekh, beta. In front. That's where we're going."
Kageaki"Yes. I had no time to stand still."

en.html:
I nodded hard at my foster mother's words. Yes. What I should do now was go forward, even if only by groping.

Standing frozen with fear because the road is dark changes nothing! Collect similar cases. From those, look for recoveries, and find out which treatments worked. There was plenty to do.

While I was staring at the garden like a fool, I should have started on whatever I could.
...I am thoroughly disgusted with my own weakness.

　同様の症例を収集する……そこから回復例を探し、

手を付けていくべきだった。
　……己の惰弱さにはほとほと呆れる。
